content.introduction: The Federal Reserve's monetary policy aims to promote maximum employment and stable prices. It primarily uses the federal funds rate and other tools to influence economic conditions. The Federal Open Market Committee sets this policy.
body:
Monetary policy in the United States comprises the Federal Reserve's actions and communications to promote maximum employment, stable prices, and moderate long-term interest rates--the economic goals the Congress has instructed the Federal Reserve to pursue.

##### 2025 Review of Monetary Policy Strategy, Tools, and Communications [...] The Federal Reserve, the central bank of the United States, provides the nation with a safe, flexible, and stable monetary and financial system.

The members of the Federal Reserve's Board of Governors in Washington, D.C., and the presidents of the regional Federal Reserve Banks participate in Federal Open Market Committee meetings. At these meetings, this group of policymakers discusses the state of the national economy as well as economic conditions prevailing across different parts of the United States, and they deliberate on an appropriate policy course to support strong labor markets and price stability. [...] The members of the Federal Reserve's Board of Governors in Washington, D.C., and the presidents of the regional Federal Reserve Banks participate in Federal Open Market Committee meetings. At these meetings, this group of policymakers discusses the state of the national economy as well as economic conditions prevailing across different parts of the United States, and they deliberate on an appropriate policy course to support strong labor markets and price stability. [...] The Fed primarily conducts monetary policy through changes in the target for the federal funds rate. To encourage short-term interest rates to move close to the target range, the Fed uses various policy tools including:

   interest on reserve balances, and
   the overnight reverse repurchase facility rate.
